title: Mutation Score Understates Oracle Provenance: Agent-Generated Test Suites on Defects4J, With and Without the Implementation
description: Two test suites were generated per Defects4J bug with the same agent and model, under two conditions: the agent either works in the project's source tree or sees only its javadoc. The comparison was run twice on the same 40 bugs. In the second campaign, with the benchmark's metadata removed from the working copy, the conditions enforced by a sandbox, every transcript kept and the analysis fixed in advance, real-fault detection falls from 56% to 18% over 39 bugs, while mutation score falls from 54% to 39% and line coverage from 84% to 70%. The first campaign, on standard Defects4J checkouts, gave 72% against 14%. Two further campaigns, under the second's conditions and protocols also fixed in advance, took the comparison to faults that postdate the model's training data. On 28 of them the arms detect 35% against 22% over 23 subjects, a difference the test does not reject (p = 0.25). On 115 more, in a tighter sandbox, they detect 19% against 3% over 112 subjects (p = 0.00004), while their mutation scores, measured with PIT, are 44% against 50% pooled and 62% against 56% as means over suites. The repository holds the generation and measurement scripts, the protocols and full records of the second, third and fourth campaigns, the per-suite measurements, an EvoSuite baseline, a hand classification of the 40 faults, a probe of what the model recalls about each fault with no code in context, two post-cutoff replication corpora and the pool of post-cutoff subjects the fourth campaign draws on, and an audit of what the benchmark's own files told the agent.
